reason: The sources provide multi-site corroboration for more than 15 atomic facts detailing the Soyuz 11 mission, mechanical failure, decompression, and aftermath.
story: In June 1971, Soviet cosmonauts Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev made history aboard Salyut 1, the world's first space station. After spending more than three weeks conducting science and setting endurance records, the crew packed up and initiated their return to Earth. As the Soyuz 11 descent module separated from the service module high above the atmosphere, explosive bolts detonated, violently jarring open an air equalization valve. In less than a minute, the cabin atmosphere vented entirely into the vacuum of space. Because the crew wore flight suits rather than pressurized spacesuits, they lost consciousness within twenty seconds and died of decompression roughly one hundred miles up. The automated capsule re-entered the atmosphere and made a gentle parachute touchdown in Kazakhstan. Recovery teams opened the hatch expecting triumphant record-breakers, but found all three men lifeless in their seats. They remain the only humans to die in space.
angle: The Soyuz 11 cosmonauts remain the only three humans ever to die in the vacuum of space, killed in under two minutes when a tiny valve popped open 100 miles up.

claims.claim: The crew of Soyuz 11 consisted of Georgy Dobrovolsky, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev.
Soyuz 11 docked with Salyut 1, the world's first crewed space station.
Soyuz 11 launched on June 6, 1971, from Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
The entire original prime crew was replaced just days before launch after Valery Kubasov was suspected of having tuberculosis.
Vladislav Volkov was the only member of the replacement crew who had flown in space before.
The crew conducted scientific experiments on Salyut 1, including growing onions and Chinese cabbage.
Viktor Patsayev became the first person to celebrate a birthday in space during the mission.
The crew experienced an electrical smoke or fire incident during their stay on the station.
Soyuz 11 undocked from Salyut 1 late on June 29, 1971, to prepare for return to Earth.
A pressure equalization ventilation valve opened inadvertently when the capsule modules separated prior to atmospheric re-entry.
The valve opened at high altitude in the vacuum of space, roughly 80 to 104 miles above Earth.
The spacecraft cabin completely depressurized into space in less than one minute.
The cosmonauts were not wearing pressurized spacesuits during re-entry.
Radio communication with the capsule abruptly stopped well before normal atmospheric entry blackout.
The descent capsule touched down automatically on parachutes in Kazakhstan.
Rescuers opened the hatch to find all three cosmonauts motionless and dead in their seats.
Search and rescue medical personnel attempted resuscitation and CPR on the cosmonauts to no avail.
The Soyuz 11 crew are the only humans to have died in space above the Karman line.
The crew received a state funeral and their ashes were interred in Moscow's Kremlin Wall Necropolis.
NASA astronaut Thomas Stafford served as a pallbearer representing the United States at the funeral.
Following the disaster, the Soyuz spacecraft was redesigned and subsequent crews were required to wear pressure suits during launch and landing.
The names of Dobrovolsky, Volkov, and Patsayev were placed on the Moon on the Fallen Astronaut plaque by the Apollo 15 mission.

disputed: Separation altitude: S1 reports 168 km (104 miles), S3 reports about 80 miles, and S4 reports around 100 miles (160 km). The script should state 'roughly 80 to 100 miles above Earth' rather than a precise single number.
Mission duration: S1 and S3 state the stay on Salyut was over 22 days (total flight 570 hours), while S6 and S7 report nearly 24 days. The script should use 'more than three weeks'.

Individual actions inside the cabin during decompression: S1 and S3 suggest Patsayev may have attempted to reach the valve under his seat, while S4 claims Dobrovolsky and Volkov unstrapped to search for the leak while Patsayev remained seated. The script should attribute specific physical actions inside the capsule as post-flight reconstructions based on body positions.

Kubasov's medical diagnosis: S3 says Kubasov was suspected of having tuberculosis which was later overturned, while S4 claims the inflammation was specifically diagnosed as a pollen allergy. The script should stick to the suspicion of tuberculosis.
